chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sad ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughira, from al-Sakuni, from Jafar ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon him). He said:

Seize the opportunity for supplication at five times: during the recitation of the Quran, during the call to prayer, when the rain falls, when two rows meet in battle for martyrdom, and during the supplication of the oppressed, for there is no barrier between it and the Throne.

key_terms.أذان: Adhan - the Islamic call to prayer
key_terms.مظلوم: Mazlum - the oppressed, one who has been wronged

ai.seo_question: What are the five best times for supplication in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS), through the chain of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), identifies five occasions when supplication is especially potent and readily accepted: during Quran recitation, during the adhan, when rain is descending, when opposing armies meet on the battlefield for martyrdom, and when an oppressed person calls out to God. The final occasion is singled out with the remarkable statement that no barrier exists between such a supplication and God's Throne, underscoring the gravity of oppression and the divine guarantee of hearing the oppressed.
